---
title: "From a panel to its analysis"
subtitle: "Three levels of reproducibility, with explicit starting points."
---

## 01 · Read the evidence

The five chapters present saved analytical results alongside their methods and
source code. Reading does not require R, Python or access to the original server.
The current website is a **documentation build**, not a fresh statistical run.

## 02 · Recreate a panel from checkpoints

The executable R Markdown documents and chapter scripts live in `analyses/`.
They expect processed inputs at chapter-relative paths. These binary inputs are
not yet included in this GitHub draft; consult the [data catalogue](datasets.qmd)
before running an analysis. A missing file must be restored from its verified
source, not substituted with rounded values read from a figure.

| Chapter | Renderer, run from the corresponding chapter directory |
|:--|:--|
| Figure 1 + S1 | `Rscript render_figure1_and_s1.R` |
| Figure 2 + S2 | `Rscript render_figure2_and_s2.R` |
| Figure 3 + S3 | `Rscript render_figure3_and_s3.R` |
| Figure 4 + S4 | `Rscript render_figure4_and_s4.R` |
| Figure 5 + S5 | `Rscript render_figure5_and_s5.R` |

Restore the inputs, match the recorded software versions, then execute in the
chapter directory. The renderer may write regenerated figures and tables there.
Do not install a new package version merely to make an old analysis run without
checking whether it changes the result.

## 03 · Repeat upstream processing

Raw-read alignment, normalisation, genome-wide model fitting and predictor
training are separate from checkpoint-to-panel reconstruction. Their source
code and provenance are being consolidated. The documentation does **not**
claim that a single command currently reproduces the entire paper from raw data.

For small RNA, distinguish nf-core/smrnaseq reprocessing from analyses that used
published processed matrices. For methylation, distinguish IDAT preprocessing
and genome-wide discovery from the compact panel-level inputs. Controlled-access
metadata must be obtained through the appropriate access process.

## Statistical comparisons are part of the result

- Keep pooled and matched controls attached to the panels that display them.
- Preserve the recorded multiple-testing family; do not reinterpret a global
  q value as a per-timepoint test.
- For the **123-CpG reference**, the Figure 4o centre tests the average matched
  displacement over T1–T6, whereas the right panel tests the T5–T6 endpoint.
  Neither label is a test of an increasing temporal slope.
- hTERT final-cycle and whole-series tests are separate endpoints.
- CpGs and repeated timepoints do not increase the number of independent runs.

## Build the documentation locally

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_docs.py
python3 scripts/check_repository.py
quarto render docs
quarto preview docs --host 127.0.0.1
```

These commands build and serve local documentation only. They do not deploy
GitHub Pages, run analyses or download data. Python 3 uses only its standard
library for the documentation preparation script.

## Release status

Before public release, we will reconcile the remaining reconstruction labels,
restore and archive the input checkpoints, record software environments and
test chapter execution. See the
[release checklist](https://github.com/BolisLab/mir29/blob/main/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md).
